stories.headline: FIFA names the hosts of the next two Women's World Cups
stories.summary: FIFA has confirmed who will stage the next two Women's World Cups. The 2031 tournament will be shared by Costa Rica, Jamaica, Mexico and the United States, and the 2035 tournament by England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales. The 2031 finals will be the first to involve 48 national teams.

stories.headline: The UN climate conference in Turkey ends without an agreement
stories.summary: The 31st United Nations climate conference, COP31, was held at the Expo Center in Antalya, Turkey. Negotiators did not work out a climate pact, divided over language relating to fossil fuels. It was the longest-running UN climate summit on record, and the first to conclude without an agreement since 2009.

stories.headline: Kenya and the Democratic Republic of the Congo restore ties
stories.summary: The president of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Félix Tshisekedi, and the president of Kenya, William Ruto, have agreed to restore full diplomatic relations. They met at a summit in Oyo, in the Republic of the Congo, hosted by President Denis Sassou Nguesso. Faure Gnassingbé, a former president of Togo, mediated.

stories.headline: A spider named for Stephen Colbert has its genome read
stories.summary: Researchers have read the genome of a trapdoor spider that lives in California's coastal dunes. Aptostichus stephencolberti carries 4.6 billion DNA base pairs, which is not the largest among spiders but is still significant. The species is Stephen Colbert's namesake in the spider world.
